se.explanation: Attenuate and mitigate both mean to reduce in force; exacerbate and bolster would increase it.

se.text: Lacking evidence against the whistleblower's claims, the company tried instead to _____ her, circulating rumors about her past.
se.explanation: Discredit and denigrate both mean to damage a person's standing, matching the rumors; substantiate and laud would help her.

se.text: The merger plan would _____ a dozen small banks into one national institution.
se.explanation: Aggregate and amalgamate both mean to combine into a single whole; the other verbs do not fit 'into one institution'.

se.text: The farmers, _____ by temperament, greeted news of both the bumper harvest and the flood with a shrug.
se.explanation: Stolid and phlegmatic both mean unexcitable, which explains the identical shrug; the others imply strong or changeable reactions.

se.text: Observers attributed the decline in volunteering to a creeping _____ among residents who no longer believed their efforts mattered.
se.explanation: Apathy and lassitude both mean listless indifference, which follows from lost belief; fervor and alacrity mean enthusiasm.

se.text: Her editorial, an intemperate _____ against the university board, cost her the goodwill of former allies.
se.explanation: Diatribe and invective both mean bitter verbal abuse, matching 'intemperate' and the loss of allies; approbation would be praise.

se.text: Instead of answering the question, the coach launched into a _____ about the lack of discipline.
se.explanation: Tirade and harangue both mean a long, angry speech; a preamble would be an introduction, which fits grammatically but not the angry sense implied.

se.text: After decades in politics, she had become _____ to even the harshest criticism.
se.explanation: Inured and impervious both mean unaffected by, which fits long exposure; the others do not take 'to criticism' in this sense.

se.text: The exhausted climbers were nearly _____ to the cold, no longer even shivering.
se.explanation: Insensible and inured both mean no longer responsive to; the others do not take 'to the cold' with this meaning.

se.text: The child's _____ questions about the bishop's wealth silenced the dinner table.
se.explanation: Artless and ingenuous both mean innocently frank, which explains the awkward silence; disingenuous and mendacious imply deceit.

se.text: Livestock bred over centuries for a _____ nature are far easier to herd than their wild ancestors.
se.explanation: Compliant and tractable both mean easily managed; recalcitrant and refractory are the opposite.

se.text: The physicist is admired for _____ explanations that make even abstruse ideas feel obvious.
se.explanation: Lucid and luminous both mean clear and illuminating here; convoluted and tortuous would obscure ideas.

se.text: Pundits who _____ the young poet's early efforts were silenced by the acclaim for her second book.
se.explanation: Deride and disparage both mean to belittle, which explains why acclaim silenced them; laud and venerate would not be silenced.

se.text: Hoping to _____ the furious landowner, the council offered a payment and a public apology.
se.explanation: Mollify and propitiate both mean to soothe an angered party with concessions; goad and foment would further anger him.

se.text: The ministry proved so _____ to outside pressure, ignoring petitions and rebuffing every delegation, that reformers gave up lobbying it.
se.explanation: Refractory and intractable both mean unresponsive to persuasion, which explains why lobbying was abandoned; tractable and compliant mean the opposite.

se.text: Even the most _____ guests found themselves unable to interrupt the host's monologue on tax policy.
se.explanation: Loquacious and verbose both mean talkative here, which makes the monologue unstoppable; laconic and reticent do not.

se.text: Although he was a fortune's heir, the poet kept an _____ household with little more than a bed, a table and a lamp.
se.explanation: Austere and abstemious both mean frugal and restrained; ostentatious and prodigal suggest display and extravagance.

se.text: The younger officers' _____ refusal to obey any order from headquarters led to a formal inquiry.
se.explanation: Obdurate and recalcitrant both mean stubbornly resistant to authority; tractable and malleable mean yielding.

se.text: The mourners listened in silence to a moving _____ in honor of the retired lighthouse keeper.
se.explanation: Eulogy and elegy both mean a tribute to one who has died or retired, fitting a moving occasion; a tirade or diatribe would be hostile.

se.text: The routine of the lab was so _____ that the discovery came as a shock to staff accustomed to uneventful days.
se.explanation: Banal and mundane both mean ordinary and unremarkable, which explains the shock; profound and esoteric suggest significance.

se.text: The new government moved quickly to _____ the previous regime's tax decrees, declaring them void from the start of the year.
se.explanation: Rescind and repudiate both mean to cancel or disown formally, fitting 'declaring them void'; sanction and bolster would uphold them.

se.text: Bacteria placed in the cold chamber became _____, ceasing to divide until warmed.
se.explanation: Inert and quiescent both mean inactive, matching 'ceasing to divide'; the other choices suggest agitation or spread.

se.text: As the night wore on and the speeches dragged, the crowd's enthusiasm began to _____.
se.explanation: Flag and abate both mean to weaken gradually, matching a dragging program; burgeon and exacerbate would increase it.

se.text: Prices for the rare dye were so _____, doubling one month and halving the next, that merchants refused long contracts.
se.explanation: Volatile and capricious both mean given to abrupt unpredictable change, matching the doubling and halving; immutable and perennial mean unchanging.
